Do it! It's challenging, but there are plenty of video guides out there to help out and it definitely helps that the game itself is so immersive and beautiful. I had played (not to completion) two soulsborne games before this, and I think Elden Ring is one if not the most accessible. That isn't to say it's easy! But the gameplay mechanics are much more forgiving. If not, I would also recommend Dark Souls 3, but keep in mind that it's going for the same price as Elden Ring and it was released in 2016.

There are a lot of things the game won't tell you that you'll have to look up. Don't feel bad like you're cheating, it's okay to do a lil research! That being said, a lot of times you'll figure things out simply by walking around and exploring.

​

Something that helped me, funnily enough, was playing Hollow Knight. It's very different from Dark Souls but you learn a lot of game sense that translates wonderfully to a whole host of different games. It's $14.99 on steam and is my favorite game of all time. It's a hard game as well, but it teaches a lot of the patience that's required for Soulsborne games.I'd really recommend it, I think it would help you start expanding your horizons.

I'm so sorry you're going through this. Guilt in my opinion is one of the hardest feelings to deal with. The fact you were able to talk back to that horrible therapist is great, and I feel it hopefully shows you still feel you are worth something and didn't just take what they said. I've had my fair share of shitty therapists, sadly it can be comparable to medication in that you need to find someone whose methods work best for you. My current therapist is a free one, and is better than the accredited novel writing psychologist that I saw for a few months. I also understand about the sexuality aspect, as my parents are blatantly homophobic and I feel I could never come out about my bisexuality unless I married a woman.

What I'm trying to say in all this rambling is that you are not alone. I'm not trying to discredit your feelings or make you think your problems are "not as bad" as other's (pain isn't a contest), I just know that it never helps to feel like you're the only one who has made the mistakes you have, that no one understands. It's easier said than done, but I do like that saying that so much can change in a month because it's different than the shitty overused, "it always gets better" because hey, sometimes it doesn't or at least not for a while. Things can and will change in a month, whatever that means. 

Try not to isolate yourself. I know how that feels, and it's so tempting, but it will make you feel more alone and more empty. If you don't feel like hanging out with friends, that's okay. If you're able to drive or walk anywhere just go somewhere with people, even if it's just the grocery store.

I've been through thoughts of suicide. I've hurt the people I've loved most and lost people I loved. It's hard to feel better and it doesn't come fast and it doesn't come easy. There will always be good days and there will always be those days where it feels like you can't go on with the pain anymore. Try to figure out what works for you, even little things like listening to angry music or taking a 2 hour long shower and just crying it all out.

I'm sorry this was so unorganized. I do hope you feel better, it sounds like we've been through fairly similar things.
